_meta.description: Context Memory bench corpus — two scenes of Japanese VN dialogue with deliberate cross-line dependencies, a verbatim-repeated line to exercise cache-hit behavior, and a scene boundary to exercise context reset.
_meta.targetLangNote: Fixed to English (en-us), not overridable via CLI. Spanish (the app's usual default) is pro-drop like Japanese, so DeepL can legally omit the subject pronoun in the elided-subject test lines regardless of whether context reached it — that would make the pronoun/gender assertions pass or fail for the wrong reason. English forces an overt subject pronoun, which is what makes those assertions diagnostic instead of noise. en-us (not bare 'en') to avoid DeepL's variant-required target_lang behavior.
_meta.windowSizeNote: Default context window size for the 'with-context' leg. The no-context leg always uses window=0. Override via --window.

scenes.label: Yuki and Hina walk to the park

lines.source: はい、行きます。
lines.note: Cache-prime: first occurrence of this exact line. Also the very first line of the whole run, so the incoming context window must be empty.

lines.source: 雪は静かに頷いて、コートを羽織った。
lines.note: Establishes the name Yuki (雪) as a person doing human actions (nodding, putting on a coat) — the antecedent the next line's elided subject depends on.

lines.source: 微笑んで、そっと囁いた。
lines.note: Elided subject — Japanese omits it entirely. Correct English translation requires inferring 'she' from A2's context. Without context, DeepL must still pick some subject (English is not pro-drop) and has no basis to prefer 'she'.

lines.source: 陽菜「星が綺麗だね」と言った。
lines.note: Filler #2 of 3 — introduces a second speaker (Hina) and an unrelated topic (stars). Exists to put distance between A1 and A5: with windowSize=2, by the time A5 is processed, A1 must already have aged out of the window (A2/A3/A4 = 3 lines of separation, > windowSize).

lines.source: はい、行きます。
lines.note: Verbatim repeat of A1 — MUST be served from cache/translation-memory, not re-sent to the engine. This is the cache-hit scenario: expectCacheHit is a precondition the bench aborts on if unmet, not a scored assertion — a corpus where this silently falls through to a live call would prove nothing about Bug A.

lines.source: どこへ？
lines.note: Depends on A5 being in the context window. THIS is the regression guard for Bug A: pipeline._doTranslate() returns early on a cache hit (pipeline.js:417-436) without ever calling engine.translate(), and the context push lives inside the engine — so today A5's cache hit never reaches the window, and this assertion is expected to FAIL until the push moves to a single site in the pipeline that also runs on cache/TM hits.

lines.source: 雪も一緒に公園まで歩いた。
lines.note: Name continuity check — 雪 (Yuki) must keep being translated as the name, not as the common noun 'snow'. Largely self-disambiguating from grammar alone, kept as a general sanity check rather than a strict context-dependency test.

lines.source: 先輩、お先に失礼します。
lines.note: Register/honorific coverage (senpai + polite leave-taking). Deliberately left without a strict assertion — how keigo maps onto English politeness markers is subjective and DeepL's rendering isn't stable enough to assert on without inflating false failures. Kept as corpus content and as a normal (non-cache) push so A9's context check has a clean antecedent.

lines.source: 「うん、また明日」と微笑んだ。
lines.note: Continuity check on the NORMAL (non-cache) path, contrasted deliberately with A6: A8 was never a cache hit, so this assertion is expected to PASS today even though A6 fails — showing the bug is isolated to the cache/TM shortcut, not the context mechanism in general.

lines.source: 二人は駅で別れた。
lines.note: Scene wrap-up. Simple, context-independent content check.

scenes.label: Takuya studies in the library
scenes.resetContextNote: The bench calls engine.clearContext() directly here (the same method that exists in deepl.js/openai.js/local-llm.js today but has zero callers anywhere in the codebase). This tests two things at once: (1) that clearContext()'s own implementation is correct — it should genuinely empty the window when invoked, which B1's contextWindowEmpty assertion confirms; (2) it gives Scene B a clean boundary so B1's content assertions test 'no leftover Yuki/female context', not 'we forgot to call the one working reset method'. It does NOT by itself prove production leaks between games — that's already established statically (zero callers, found by grep) and is exactly what Fase 2 (automatic reset on profile load / language change / engine change) exists to fix.

lines.source: 机に向かって、黙々と問題集を解いていた。
lines.note: Elided subject, first line of a new scene with no name given yet. If context leaked from Scene A, an MT engine could plausibly lean female/Yuki; with a real reset, there is nothing to lean on.

lines.source: 分かりました、頑張ります。
lines.note: Cache-prime for the second cache-hit scenario, in a different scene than A1/A5 to confirm the bug isn't specific to Scene A's setup.

lines.source: 拓也は時計を見て、ため息をついた。
lines.note: Introduces the name Takuya (拓也), male — the scene's protagonist for the name-continuity checks.

lines.source: 「あと十分か……」と机の上の参考書を睨んだ。
lines.note: Normal-path context check (B3 was never a cache hit), mirrors A3/A9.

lines.source: 隣の席の友人が、小さく笑った。
lines.note: Filler #3 of 3 — same purpose as A4: puts 3 lines of separation between B2 and B6 so B2 ages out of a windowSize=2 window before the repeat.

lines.source: 分かりました、頑張ります。
lines.note: Verbatim repeat of B2 — second independent cache-hit scenario.

lines.source: 拓也はそう答えて、また問題に向き直った。
lines.note: Regression guard for Bug A, second instance in a different scene — expected to FAIL today for the same reason as A6.

lines.source: 先生が教室に入ってきた。
lines.note: Filler, introduces a neutral third character (teacher) — no gender-continuity claim attached, deliberately.

lines.source: 「静かに」と先生は言った。
lines.note: Normal-path context check, mirrors A9/B4.

lines.source: 拓也たちは静かに席についた。
lines.note: Scene wrap-up and final name-continuity check across the whole scene.
